To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have characterized a FMO protein of a newly discovered aerobic chlorophytotroph, Candidat Chloracidobacteriurn thermophilum, which has a different spectral signature than that of the FMO of green sulfur bacteria, and that this FMO protein has conserved residues that bind BChl molecules, suggesting that the protein probably binds seven or possibly even eight BChl molecules.

the FMO protein in the chlorophototrophic bacterium Cab. thermophilium, a member of the Acidobacteria phylum, is a homodimeric protein that binds BChl a and has a spectroscopic signature that is distinct from the FMO proteins of green sulfur bacteria.

the FMO protein isolated from Cab. thermophilumspectroscopic properties differ from that of the FMO of green sulfur bacteria and that the residues known to be involved in BChl a binding are conserved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the FMO proteins of Cab. thermphilum.
the characterization of the FMO from an aerobic chlorophototropic Acidobacteria.
the elucidation of the molecular basis for the unique properties of the Cab. thermophilum FMO.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Cab. thermophilums FMO is a homologous protein to the FMO protein in GSB but that the FMO protein exhibits some unique features that may allow it to perform efficient light harvesting in an aerobic habitat.

the FMO protein in Cab. thermophilumserves the same function as in GSB, namely, to transfer excitation energy to the RC, but that the protein has adapted to the aerobic environment in which it operates by acquiring properties which allow it to function more efficiently in that environment.
the Cab. thermophillum FMO protein is a novel member of the FMO family, but the exact role of FMO protein in Cab. thermophilus is still not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Cab. thermphilum FMO protein has the ability to harvest light efficiently under aerobic conditions by having a different pigment composition and a weaker pigment-pigment interaction than that in GSB.
the Cab. thermophile FMO has a unique structure, which allows it to efficiently perform light harvesting in aerobic environments.
the FMO protein can be used to adapt a photosynthetic apparatus to a wide variety of environmental conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FMO protein, a key component in light harvesting, has the capacity to adapt to a wide range of environments.
the FMO protein can be adapted to function under a wide range of environmental conditions.
Cab. thermophilums FMO protein, despite its unusual spectral properties, is likely to function as a light harvesting antenna protein in the same way as FMO in other chlorophototrophic bacteria.
